body: Kentucky Industrial Alliance LLC owns a large tract in Cave City, Kentucky, where it is seeking to build a large-scale data center with a developer, the OTN Group, the Bowling Green Daily News reported. The company says it owns more than 600 acres in the area and submitted a development plan to the Joint City-County Planning Commission of Barren County on May 11, 2026, according to Glasgow News 1's account of its complaint. After special-called meetings on May 18 and May 20, the Cave City Council approved a 12-month moratorium on data centers.

The company sued the city, the council and the planning commission in Barren Circuit Court on June 8, 2026, asking for an injunction against the moratorium and for its application to be reviewed under the zoning rules in place when it was filed. It argues it acquired vested rights before the moratorium and that the city skipped procedures required by Kentucky planning law, Glasgow News 1 reported. Cave City has moved to dismiss, contending the challenge lacks merit and rests on incomplete application paperwork.

A second suit, also filed in June, seeks to invalidate Cave City's annexation of the land, alleging that city officials did not obtain written consent from the owner of a small cemetery within the tract. The city counters that the company lacks standing because the annexation has not harmed its interests. At the first hearing in both cases, on August 24, the parties generally agreed to consolidate them, with Judge John T. Alexander to decide annexation first. "If the property was not appropriately annexed then the moratorium wouldn't apply to that property anyway," city attorney Aaron Smith told the Daily News. Discovery on annexation is under way, and a status conference is set for November 23, 2026.

timeline.label: Kentucky Industrial Alliance submits a development plan to the planning commission
Cave City Council holds special-called meetings and approves a 12-month data-center moratorium
Kentucky Industrial Alliance sues over the moratorium
Company files a second suit challenging the annexation of its land
Parties agree to consolidate; Judge John T. Alexander will decide annexation first
Status conference to consider a briefing schedule on annexation
